product.name: Spendwise
product.vision: A Finance Lite backend that lets an individual manage accounts, record transactions, categorize spending, set budgets, transfer money atomically, handle recurring transactions, import CSV statements, auto-apply categorization rules, and view a dashboard/report — built incrementally from a pure-Java domain to a production backend, with optional AI acting only as an advisory layer.
outOfScope: support for every bank file format

releases.title: Java Domain
releases.problem: Spendwise has no domain yet; there is no safe way to represent money, accounts, or transactions, and financial invariants (valid amount/type/account) are unprotected.
releases.goal: Build the core Spendwise domain in pure Java with encapsulated invariants — no Spring, no database, no REST.
acceptanceCriteria: Can create an Account
Can create a Transaction
Basic business invariants are protected inside the domain
Money uses BigDecimal (never double/float for business amounts)
No dependency on Spring, database, or REST

releases.title: Java Application
releases.problem: The domain objects exist but there is no working application around them — no way to store, search, aggregate, or persist transactions between runs.
releases.goal: Turn the domain into a small working Java application with an in-memory repository, transaction service, basic statistics, and simple CSV read/write.
acceptanceCriteria: Can manage transactions in memory
Can search transactions
Can group by category and total income/expense
Can save/load simple data via CSV
Concurrency applied only when a natural use case exists (not forced)

releases.title: Spring Boot Core
releases.problem: The Java application wires its own dependencies manually and cannot grow into a real backend without an application container and configuration.
releases.goal: Migrate the application onto Spring Boot with IoC/DI-managed service and repository beans, reusing the existing domain unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Application boots on Spring Boot
Existing Java domain is reused, not rewritten
Business logic is not rewritten just because of the Spring migration
Beans are managed via IoC/DI

releases.title: REST API
releases.problem: Spendwise can only be driven from code/CLI; there is no HTTP surface for creating accounts, recording transactions, or managing categories.
releases.goal: Expose Spendwise over an HTTP REST API with DTOs, bean validation, and consistent error responses.
acceptanceCriteria: Can create an account via HTTP
Can create, list and filter transactions via HTTP
Can manage categories via HTTP
Inputs validated via DTO + Bean Validation
Errors returned consistently (ProblemDetail / RFC 7807)
Frontend not yet required (Swagger/Postman usable)

releases.title: Persistence
releases.problem: Restarting the application loses all data, and transfers between two accounts can leave balances inconsistent if only one side succeeds.
releases.goal: Persist financial data in PostgreSQL via Spring Data JPA and make account transfer atomic with rollback on failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Data survives application restart
Transfer (Account A -500000 / Account B +500000) is atomic
An incomplete/invalid transfer rolls back entirely

releases.title: Security & Ownership
releases.problem: The API is open: any caller can read or modify any account, transaction, or budget — Spendwise is not a real multi-user backend.
releases.goal: Make Spendwise a proper multi-user backend with register/login/JWT authentication and backend-enforced resource ownership.
acceptanceCriteria: Register/login issue JWT and protected endpoints require it
Ownership is checked on the backend, not the frontend
User A cannot read/update/delete User B's Account, Transaction, or Budget

releases.title: Business Engine
releases.problem: Spendwise is still essentially CRUD; it lacks the budgeting, recurring, and rule logic that make it an actual finance product. V0.7-V1.0 are not part of the 40-lesson course: they are a suggested self-study/OJT continuation - the formal course is complete at V0.6, and the Day 39-64 OJT window is the primary suggested execution window from this release onward (recommended, not required).
releases.goal: Push Spendwise beyond CRUD with Budget, Recurring Transaction, a Rule engine, and advanced statistics via domain services.
acceptanceCriteria: Budget computes limit / spent / remaining / percentage / status per category+period
Budget overrun does not delete or edit real transactions
Recurring transaction has next due date, frequency, active status and avoids duplicates
Rule engine applies categorization by conditions/actions/priority
Advanced statistics/aggregation available

releases.title: Data Processing
releases.problem: Users cannot bring real statement data in; importing the same CSV twice would create uncontrolled duplicates and failures could leave the system in an unclear state.
releases.goal: Process real transaction data via CSV import with an ImportBatch, validation, deduplication, an import result, optional background import for large datasets, and CSV export.
acceptanceCriteria: Import reports successful, duplicate, and failed rows
Importing the same transaction multiple times does not create uncontrolled duplicates
Import failure does not leave the system in an unclear state
CSV export is available
Large datasets can be imported as a background job (optional, ImportBatch status)

releases.title: Production Engineering
releases.problem: Dashboard aggregation is recomputed on every request, recurring transactions are not generated automatically, there is no external FX data, and the system lacks tests, observability, and a reproducible environment.
releases.goal: Bring Spendwise close to a production backend: reference-data caching (Redis optional) with correct invalidation, recurring scheduler, external exchange-rate API, testing, OpenAPI, logging, monitoring, and Docker.
acceptanceCriteria: Reference/category data is cached with correct invalidation (dashboard figures are never cached - R11; the Redis backend is an optional swap)
Recurring scheduler runs periodically without creating duplicates
External exchange rate fetched via RestClient/WebClient with retry/failure handling
Unit and integration tests (Testcontainers) pass
Health check and metrics exposed (Actuator/Micrometer)
Application runs in a Dockerized environment

releases.title: Smart Finance
releases.problem: Core functionality needs final stabilization, and there is an opportunity to add valuable intelligent features without letting AI take over business rules.
releases.goal: Stabilize all core functionality and add optional AI category suggestion and monthly insight as an advisory layer, plus portfolio-readiness.
acceptanceCriteria: All core features stable
AI category suggestion only suggests; user confirms before data changes
AI monthly insight turns backend-aggregated numbers into natural language (LLM does not query DB or compute business numbers)
AI never transfers money, edits transactions/budgets, or deletes data
Portfolio README, final demo, and test coverage delivered

reject operations across mismatched currencies (R4)

buildTasks.title: Account domain object with protected balance

constraints: login returns a token produced through a TokenIssuer interface
the interface has NO signing implementation in the learner's code yet - a test double stands in until the canonical issuer lands
after logout the same token is rejected with 401 (day-24 required group)
the JWT carries identity only (R23)

acceptanceCriteria: login returns a token produced via the TokenIssuer interface
after logout the same token gets 401
no signing implementation exists behind the interface yet

the JWT carries identity only (R23)

replay of a rotated token is detected and rejected

buildTasks.title: Budget model with period-scoped limits
buildTasks.problem: Spendwise can record spending but cannot express 'at most X per category per month', so the learner has no target to steer against and no data substrate for the later calculation task.
buildTasks.goal: A Budget entity/aggregate keyed by category + period (YearMonth-shaped VARCHAR(7)) carrying the limit as Money, stored by a new Flyway migration, with ownership and invariant fields but no computed figures.
constraints: limit is Money (BigDecimal, R1) and the DDL column is NUMERIC(19,2) declared in the migration (R3), not in @Column
period is a YearMonth-shaped VARCHAR(7) key (R12), never two ints and never a bare LocalDateTime
no spent/remaining/percentage/status fields exist on the stored model - those are derived at read time in task-budget-calculation (R10)
one Budget per (user, category, period) - enforce with a new versioned Flyway migration, never by editing V1/V2 (R26)
every Budget row carries user_id from the start (R25)
budget domain/service classes live in com.spendwise.budget (R13)
acceptanceCriteria: a Budget can be created for a category + month with a positive Money limit and rejects a non-positive or wrong-currency limit
the schema change arrives as a new versioned Flyway migration and ddl-auto: validate still boots the app against it
two budgets for the same user+category+period are rejected by a UNIQUE constraint
no derived financial figure (spent/remaining/percentage/status) is stored anywhere on the Budget row

buildTasks.title: Budget spent/remaining/percentage/status computed at read time
buildTasks.problem: The stored Budget has a limit but no figures, and Spendwise must never store derived financial state - an overrun must not delete or edit transactions, and a stale stored 'spent' would lie after any transaction edit.
buildTasks.goal: A BudgetCalculationService that derives limit/spent/remaining/percentage/status per category+period from the transaction ledger at read time, exposed through a read endpoint, with no writes to transactions.
constraints: spent/remaining/percentage/status are derived at read time and never stored (R10)
spent sums EXPENSE transactions of the budget's category and period via the repository/ledger - the transaction ledger stays the sole financial truth (R6, R7)
all summation is BigDecimal: stream().map(...).reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add) - never summingDouble, never double/float (R1)
division for percentage names an explicit scale and RoundingMode at the call site (R5)
an overrun changes nothing outside the read model - no transaction or balance mutation on any budget path (R21 boundary)
read paths are readOnly = true transactions (R18)
the service returns a read model/DTO, never an entity or VO across HTTP (R16, R17)
acceptanceCriteria: a budget's spent equals a hand-computed SUM over the same period (plan §9 flow 5)
remaining/percentage/status are consistent with limit and spent at scale 2 with one explicit rounding at division
creating, editing or deleting transactions after a budget read is reflected on the next read without any cache/refresh action
a user's budget read returns 404 for another user's budget id and never leaks another user's figures (R24)
no budget path writes a Transaction, mutates a balance projection, or stores a derived figure

buildTasks.title: Recurring transaction template model
buildTasks.problem: Rent, subscriptions and salaries repeat, but Spendwise can only record them one by one, so the learner must re-enter identical transactions and will eventually forget one.
buildTasks.goal: A RecurringTransaction template entity (amount as Money, typed direction, frequency, next due date, active flag, optional end date) persisted by a new Flyway migration, with no generation logic yet.
constraints: amount is Money, always positive, with the direction carried by a typed field (R7)
nextDueDate and end date are LocalDate / DATE columns, never timestamps and never bare LocalDateTime (R12)
frequency is a closed enum (e.g. WEEKLY/MONTHLY) modeled like the fixed domain sets at day-07
the template stores no generated-transaction history itself - generated rows are ordinary Transactions and the template only advances its own nextDueDate
persisted via a new versioned Flyway migration (R26) with user_id from the start (R25)
domain classes live in com.spendwise.recurring (R13)
acceptanceCriteria: a recurring template can be created with amount, direction, frequency and nextDueDate and rejects non-positive amounts and untyped directions
nextDueDate persists as a DATE and round-trips exactly
the schema arrives as a new versioned Flyway migration and ddl-auto: validate boots against it
deactivating a template is a flag change on the template - it never deletes or edits generated transactions

buildTasks.title: Recurring generation through the canonical transaction path
buildTasks.problem: Recurring templates exist but produce nothing, and naive generation is the easiest place in Spendwise to silently duplicate financial truth - the same period generating twice would corrupt the ledger and every derived figure downstream.
buildTasks.goal: A RecurringGenerationService that materializes due occurrences as real Transactions through TransactionCreationService.create(CreateTransactionCommand), advances the template's nextDueDate only after the row exists, and is idempotent per period - the same recurring period never generates twice.
constraints: every generated Transaction goes through TransactionCreationService.create(CreateTransactionCommand) and carries a sourceRef - never a direct repository insert (R20)

sourceRef for a generated occurrence is deterministic (template id + occurrence due date shape), so re-running generation for the same period is a no-op by construction: the pre-check finds the existing row and creates nothing. The hard race guard (UNIQUE (user_id, source_ref)) arrives in V0.8's V9 migration - until then re-runs are safe only because generation is single-writer (ADR-007: the pre-check is the friendly path, the constraint is the arbiter)
the template's nextDueDate advances only inside the same transaction that created the occurrence - a crash between the two leaves either both or neither (R8/R21 atomicity discipline)
generation creates INCOME/EXPENSE rows with positive amounts and typed direction (R7) and updates balances only through the projection rules (R8)
generation is a plain service method callable from tests and, later, from the V0.9 scheduler (task-recurring-scheduler) - this task wires no scheduling of its own
an inactive template generates nothing; a past end date generates nothing
no external calls, no async dispatch inside the generation transaction (R19)
acceptanceCriteria: a due monthly template generates exactly one transaction with a deterministic sourceRef and advances nextDueDate by one frequency step
calling generation twice for the same period produces no second transaction (plan §9 flow 8)
a failed creation leaves the template's nextDueDate unchanged - no phantom advancement
a generated row is indistinguishable in kind from a manual row created through the same canonical path (same invariants, same projections)

buildTasks.title: Categorization rule model and storage
buildTasks.problem: Users categorize every import and manual entry by hand; Spendwise needs persisted rules (condition -> action, ordered) before any engine can apply them, and the rule structure must stay inside the actual domain rather than becoming a generic workflow engine.
buildTasks.goal: A CategorizationRule entity (priority, one condition predicate over transaction description/category shape, one target category action, enabled flag) persisted by a new Flyway migration - the Strategy-ready substrate for the V0.7 engine and the V0.8 import pipeline.
constraints: a rule is condition + action + priority + enabled - no generic workflow/expression language, no scriptable DSL: this stays Spendwise's own domain (master plan: no complex DSL; blueprint §5 V0.7 scope, D10/R-DEP-2)
rules are ordered by an explicit priority integer; ties resolve deterministically by a stable secondary key (e.g. id), never by database return order
priority is unique per user so ordering is total and reproducible
persisted via a new versioned Flyway migration (R26) with user_id from the start (R25)
domain classes live in com.spendwise.rule (R13); the rule model imports nothing from Spring MVC/Security (R14)
day-05's Strategy shape (an interface + implementations selected by data, not if-chains) is the intended application shape for the engine that consumes these rows
acceptanceCriteria: a rule can be created with a condition, a target category and an integer priority, and rejects duplicate priorities for the same user
priority order survives restart and is independent of insertion order
the schema arrives as a new versioned Flyway migration and ddl-auto: validate boots against it
no execution/audit fields exist yet - applying rules is task-rule-engine's concern, this task only stores them

buildTasks.title: Priority-ordered rule engine applied at transaction creation
buildTasks.problem: Rules exist as rows but nothing applies them, so categorization stays manual; a naive application that mutates financial truth directly, or that runs in nondeterministic order, would make Spendwise's results irreproducible.
buildTasks.goal: A RuleEngine service that evaluates a user's enabled rules in priority order against a transaction's description (and category shape), applies the first (highest-priority) matching rule by setting the target category, and is deterministic and side-effect-bounded.
constraints: rules apply in priority order, deterministically (plan §9 flow 9) - same input, same rule order, same outcome every time
the engine reads rules and transactions through repositories/services only; it calls no other domain subsystem - read-only consumer discipline (blueprint R-DEP-4)
application happens inside the transaction-creation flow's own transactional scope, not as an after-commit surprise; it never dispatches events or async work (R19, ADR-006)
a rule application changes ONLY the category of the transaction being created - it never edits amounts, dates, balances or other transactions (R6/R7 boundary)
Strategy shape: the condition is an implementation behind a small interface fed by the rule row - not a growing if/else chain (day-05)

a transaction that matches no rule keeps its manually assigned category - manual assignment wins when no rule matches, and an explicitly chosen category is not silently overwritten by a later re-match
no money arithmetic anywhere in the engine (R1 boundary is untouched by it)
acceptanceCriteria: with three rules of priorities 1/2/3 all matching one description, the outcome is identical across repeated runs and equals the priority-1 rule's target
a transaction whose description matches no rule keeps its explicitly assigned category
rule application never mutates amount, direction, occurredOn, balances or any transaction other than the one being created
a disabled rule is never evaluated; a rule whose target category was deleted is skipped safely without failing creation

buildTasks.title: Dashboard read model (month/category aggregates)
buildTasks.problem: Spendwise has per-category statistics from V0.2 but no single read model that answers 'how am I doing this month' across accounts, categories and budgets. Every figure recomputes from the ledger at request time (R11) - exactly why the numbers stay trustworthy, and exactly why a well-defined read model is worth building. No cache belongs to this task; V0.9's optional cache holds reference data, never the dashboard (R11).
buildTasks.goal: A DashboardReadService producing a month-scoped aggregate read model (total income/expense, per-category breakdown, per-account balances view, budget statuses) assembled from the ledger via aggregation queries and derived at request time, exposed as one read endpoint - R11 keeps every figure uncached.
constraints: every aggregate figure is derived at read time and never stored (R6, R10); the per-account balance view reads the stored R8 projection rather than recomputing it - the read model is a response record, not a persisted cache
sums are BigDecimal via reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add) over the grouping - never summingDouble, never double/float (R1)
GROUP BY-style aggregation queries live in repositories (@Query) or stream groupingBy over loaded rows - groupingBy is fine for grouping, the sum half stays BigDecimal (day-10/day-21)
no money value is cached at this layer - caching arrives only in V0.9 behind @Cacheable and still never holds money (R11)
read paths are readOnly = true (R18); the endpoint returns a record, never an entity (R16, R17)
the read model is scoped to the requesting user - every contributing query filters by owner (R24, R25)
this task implements no caching and no scheduler - V0.9 consumes it later
acceptanceCriteria: the dashboard's month totals equal a hand-computed SUM over the same transactions (blueprint §5 V0.7 Done-when)
per-category breakdown covers exactly the categories with transactions in the period, with no phantom zero rows
another user's data never appears in the response, verified with two seeded users
the response is a record assembled at request time; no dashboard figure is persisted or cached by this task

buildTasks.title: Advanced statistics: trends and top categories
buildTasks.problem: V0.2's aggregation answers 'how much per category this month' but not 'how is spending moving month over month' or 'where does most money go' - the analytical layer that makes the V0.7 dashboard genuinely useful.
buildTasks.goal: An advanced statistics service computing multi-month trends, month-over-month deltas and top-N categories by spend, via aggregation queries over the ledger, exposed as read methods on the existing statistics service, verified through tests - no new HTTP surface in this task.
constraints: every aggregation is BigDecimal end-to-end - reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add) for sums, explicit scale + RoundingMode for any average/division (R1, R5)
grouping via Collectors.groupingBy (day-10) or @Query GROUP BY (day-21) is fine for the grouping half; the value half never uses summingDouble (R1)
all reads are derived at request time from the ledger (R6, R10) and scoped to the requesting user (R24)
read paths are readOnly = true (R18); responses are records (R16)
no caching in this task - R11's boundary holds permanently; V0.9's cache is optional, non-authoritative, and still never holds money
do not parallelize these aggregations - the volumes are small and day-12's parallel idioms buy nothing here (and are outright forbidden on the V0.8 import path)
acceptanceCriteria: a 3-month trend for one category equals a hand-computed per-month SUM sequence
top-N categories by expense for a month are returned in descending spend order with exact BigDecimal totals
a user with no transactions in a month receives an empty/zero trend entry rather than an error
no aggregation result is stored or cached by this task

buildTasks.title: Sequential CSV statement parser with typed row records
buildTasks.problem: Real bank statements arrive as files, not API calls; day-12's pipeline teaches reading large CSVs, but Spendwise has no way to turn a raw statement row into a validated candidate record, and the naive reflex - parallelize the parse - would make row identity order-dependent later in this release.
buildTasks.goal: A CsvStatementParser that reads an uploaded CSV sequentially in source-file order via Files.lines, skips the header, trims BOM/quoting, and emits typed parsed-row records (raw fields plus a flag for whether the row carries a stable source reference) without touching the database.
constraints: the parse loop is sequential and processes rows in source-file order - parallelStream() and .parallel() are forbidden anywhere on the import path (R22 second clause): row identity later in this release is order-derived for the fallback tier
reading uses sequential Files.lines consumption (day-11/day-12), charset declared explicitly (day-11 path-traversal/charset teaching)

quoted-comma handling and BOM trimming go beyond the lessons: day-12's parseLine is a naive line.split(",", -1) with no quoted-field awareness (RFC 4180 parsing is not taught) - treat them as a disclosed extension of the day-12 base, implemented inside this parser, not a drop-in CSV library
the parser produces an immutable record per row with the raw string fields and NO decision-making about validity, duplicates or persistence - it parses, nothing else (R13 layering)
each parsed row exposes whether a stable source-provided reference exists (the sourceTxnId column presence), because that selects identity tier in task-duplicate-detection
no repository, no @Transactional, no service call inside parsing (R19 discipline: file I/O stays outside transactions)
classes live in com.spendwise.imports (R13: the import package is imports)
acceptanceCriteria: a 3-row sample statement parses into 3 parsed-row records in file order, header skipped
a row whose description contains a comma inside quotes parses as one row, not two
the parsed record for a row carrying a source reference exposes it; a row without one exposes none
the parser is unit-testable without Spring or a database and never writes anything

buildTasks.title: ImportBatch and ImportRow history records
buildTasks.problem: An import that fails halfway must leave a visible, queryable record of what happened per row - but if the batch model leaks into transaction identity, a re-upload generates fresh keys and duplicate detection silently dies (the defect the planning reconciliation proved in detail).
buildTasks.goal: ImportBatch and ImportRow entities persisted by a new Flyway migration, carrying user_id, file name, the import source identifier (source_key, the Level-1 sourceKey for row identity), per-row status OK/DUPLICATE/FAILED with row number and reason - explicitly history and reporting data whose PKs are never identity inputs.
constraints: ImportBatch and ImportRow are import history and reporting ONLY - their primary keys never participate in row identity (R22, D10.1); batchId and rowNo exist for the error list and summary display
every row status is exactly one of OK / DUPLICATE / FAILED (R22 terminal-state rule)
persisted via a new versioned Flyway migration (R26) with user_id from the start (R25)
ImportRow records the row number in source-file order and a human-readable failure reason
entities live in com.spendwise.imports (R13); no link from Transaction back to ImportRow - the association is one-directional provenance
no identity or fingerprint fields are stored on ImportRow beyond display data - identity is recomputed, never persisted as truth
acceptanceCriteria: an import batch row is created with user_id, original file name and a timestamp, and persists across restart
an ImportRow can record status OK, DUPLICATE or FAILED with its source-file row number and reason
the schema arrives as a new versioned Flyway migration and ddl-auto: validate boots against it
nothing on ImportBatch or ImportRow is an input to transaction identity - deleting a batch record leaves previously created transactions intact

buildTasks.title: Per-row import transaction through the canonical creation path
buildTasks.problem: One malformed row in a 5000-row bank export must not discard the other 4999, and every row that DOES commit must be indistinguishable from a hand-entered transaction - direct repository inserts would skip validation, balance projections and provenance.
buildTasks.goal: An import row processor where each parsed row is one @Transactional service call: valid rows are created through TransactionCreationService.create(CreateTransactionCommand), failures roll back that row alone and are recorded FAILED, and committed siblings are untouched.
constraints: unit of atomicity is ONE row: each row is processed in its own @Transactional service call - the batch is never atomic (R22)
every created transaction goes through TransactionCreationService.create(CreateTransactionCommand) and carries a sourceRef - import never inserts a transaction directly (R20)
a failed row records FAILED with its row number and reason, commits nothing, and never blocks its siblings (R22)
a row that is decided duplicate records DUPLICATE, creates no transaction, applies no rule, and touches no balance projection
a CSV negative amount for an EXPENSE becomes type EXPENSE + positive amount - never a negative stored amount (R7)
the caller loop consumes the parser sequentially and passes rows to the per-row transactional processor in file order (R22 second clause)
no external calls or async dispatch inside any row transaction (R19)

the row's OK/DUPLICATE/FAILED record is written outside the row's rolled-back creation transaction - by the caller loop after the per-row call returns, or in its own short transaction (day-20 REQUIRES_NEW) - so a failed row still reaches its terminal state (R22)
acceptanceCriteria: a 100-row file with 3 malformed rows yields a COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS batch, 97 committed transactions and 3 FAILED rows carrying row numbers and reasons (blueprint §5 V0.8 done-when)
a failed row leaves no transaction, no balance change and no rule application - and the rows before and after it commit normally
every committed imported transaction carries a sourceRef and went through the canonical creation service (assert via the service's own test seam, not by inserting directly)
an imported EXPENSE with a bank-side negative amount is stored as positive amount + EXPENSE direction

buildTasks.title: Two-tier row identity: source reference preferred, fingerprint+occurrence fallback
buildTasks.problem: Re-uploading the same statement must add zero transactions - but a batch PK as identity dies on re-upload, and a bare content fingerprint collapses two byte-identical LEGITIMATE rows into one, silently losing a real transaction. The identity has to be a stable source reference when the file provides one, and otherwise content plus the row's occurrence position among its own duplicates.
buildTasks.goal: A RowIdentityService computing sourceRef per the frozen two-tier model: Level 1 IMPORT:SRC:<sourceKey>:<accountId>:<normalize(sourceTxnId)> when the row carries a stable source reference; Level 2 IMPORT:<baseFingerprint>|OCC:<occurrenceIndex> with the occurrence counter keyed by base fingerprint via Map.merge, walked in source-file order.
constraints: Level 1 (preferred, order-independent): sourceRef = IMPORT:SRC: + sourceKey + : + accountId + : + normalize(sourceTxnId), where sourceKey is the import source identifier recorded on the ImportBatch (one per import pipeline/source, set when the batch is created) - normalize is trim, collapse internal whitespace to single space, uppercase

Level 2 (fallback): baseFingerprint = accountId | occurredOn | direction | amount(scale 2, toPlainString) | normalize(description), joined with | which normalize cannot emit; occurrenceIndex is the 1-based occurrence of the SAME baseFingerprint within the current statement counted in source-file order; sourceRef = IMPORT: + baseFingerprint + |OCC: + occurrenceIndex

the occurrence counter is a plain HashMap merged with counts.merge(baseFingerprint, 1, Integer::sum) (day08-blk-27) - incremented as the file is walked sequentially, never in parallel (R22 second clause)
amount uses toPlainString() at DDL scale so 100.5 and 100.50 yield one identity; occurredOn is the DATE, never an ingestion timestamp
neither identity tier is hashed - plain concatenation only (no taught way to render a digest as a string; no mandatory hashing)

the DB constraint UNIQUE (user_id, source_ref) on the transaction table is spelled out in a new migration and is the FINAL race-safe guard - the pre-check is optional politeness, the constraint decides (day-21 teaching extends to two-column UNIQUE)

a duplicate is decided by catching the constraint violation at insert time (DataIntegrityViolationException - not in the corpus, this task introduces it by name) or by the pre-check; the constraint remains the arbiter under two concurrent uploads

the LIMITATION is disclosed in code and guidance: Level 2 is stable for re-importing the same logical statement ordering only; arbitrary reordering/reconstruction of a file without source references may shift occurrence indices - this is not universal bank-file deduplication
batchId and rowNo are never inputs to identity (R22)
acceptanceCriteria: importing a statement whose rows all carry a stable source reference, twice, adds N transactions then 0, and reports N DUPLICATE rows on the second run

importing a statement with no source reference that contains two byte-identical data rows adds 2 transactions (OCC:1, OCC:2), not 1 - and re-importing the same file in the same order adds 0 and reports 2 DUPLICATE rows
re-uploading a statement in which some rows previously failed: previously-successful rows report DUPLICATE and insert nothing; previously-failed rows insert cleanly
100.5 and 100.50 in two uploads produce the same sourceRef (toPlainString at scale 2)
the transaction table migration declares UNIQUE (user_id, source_ref) and a second concurrent upload of the same file cannot double-insert (one loses at the constraint)

buildTasks.title: Rule engine applied to imported rows
buildTasks.problem: Imported rows arrive uncategorized; V0.7 built the priority-ordered rule engine for exactly this - but if import applies rules through a side door, imported and manual transactions diverge in behavior and the rule engine's invariants no longer hold for half the ledger.
buildTasks.goal: Wire the V0.7 RuleEngine into the import row processor so every imported row that becomes a transaction is categorized by the same priority-ordered rules inside the same canonical creation flow, with duplicate rows applying no rule at all.
constraints: rule application happens inside the row's own creation flow through TransactionCreationService.create(...) - import adds no separate rule pass outside it (R20)
a DUPLICATE row applies no rule and touches nothing (R22: the row outcome is terminal)
the same determinism rules as V0.7 hold: priority order, disabled rules skipped, manual-category preservation irrelevant here (imported rows arrive uncategorized)
a rule whose target category was deleted is skipped without failing the row (same soft-skip as V0.7)
no new rule capability is introduced in this task - it is wiring, not redesign (R-DEP-4: read-only consumer of the rule engine)
acceptanceCriteria: an imported row whose description matches the user's priority-1 rule lands in that rule's target category
an imported row matching no rule lands uncategorized, exactly like a manual row matching no rule
a DUPLICATE row shows no rule application of any kind
imported and manually created transactions with the same description match the same rules

buildTasks.title: Import batch summary and per-row report endpoint
buildTasks.problem: A batch that reached a terminal state is only useful if the user can SEE what happened - which rows committed, which were duplicates, which failed and why - and none of that history may leak another user's data or expose internal identity mechanics as if they were transaction data.
buildTasks.goal: A read endpoint returning the import batch summary (total / imported / duplicate / failed counts plus per-row outcomes with row numbers and reasons) assembled from ImportBatch/ImportRow history, exposed through an owned, user-scoped API.
constraints: the report distinguishes OK / DUPLICATE / FAILED per row and states the retry semantics of each (R22 terminal states)
batchId and rowNo are DISPLAYED here - this is exactly the reporting surface they exist for (R22), while identity stays out of the report's claims
the endpoint is scoped to the requesting user: another user's batch id returns 404 (R24)
read path is readOnly = true (R18); the response is a record, never an entity (R16)
the summary is derived from ImportRow rows at read time - no counters are cached or precomputed into the batch row beyond what the batch update itself writes
no identity/fingerprint mechanics are exposed as API fields beyond what the report contract needs for display
acceptanceCriteria: GET for a completed batch returns total, imported, duplicate and failed counts that sum to the row count, plus per-row status/rowNumber/reason
the response for the two-identical-rows scenario shows both rows OK with distinct row numbers (occurrence handling visible in display data only)
another user's batch id returns 404 and never leaks row data
the report is a pure read: fetching it never changes batch or row state

buildTasks.title: CSV export of the transaction ledger
buildTasks.problem: Users need their data back out - tax prep, accountant handoff, backup - and V0.2's basic CSV round-trip never addressed quoting, encoding or scoping; export is read-side reporting and must never be confused with import idempotency.
buildTasks.goal: An export endpoint streaming the user's transactions (scoped, ordered, correctly quoted) as a CSV download with an explicit charset, reusing day-26's CSV escaping and download teaching.
constraints: export is read-only reporting - it writes no transaction, no balance, no identity field (R6, R10)
export identity has NOTHING to do with import idempotency: the export carries no sourceRef/OCC semantics, and this task must not describe the export as dedup-relevant
amounts serialize at scale 2 via the existing Money formatting - no double conversion, no scientific notation (R1)
CSV fields are escaped per day-26's CSV teaching (quoting fields containing commas/quotes/newlines); charset declared explicitly (day-11)
the export streams per-user scoped rows (R24) and is readOnly = true (R18)
the download response follows day-26's Content-Disposition/download teaching; the service returns the file bytes and never a ResponseEntity (R17), and no entity crosses the HTTP boundary (R16)
acceptanceCriteria: exporting a user with transactions containing commas, quotes and Vietnamese diacritics in descriptions produces a file that re-parses to the same field values
exported amounts appear at scale 2 in plain notation for a seeded ledger of mixed amounts
the export contains only the requesting user's rows - verified with two seeded users
exporting does not modify any transaction, balance or import record

buildTasks.title: Optional asynchronous large-import path (no HTTP contract change)
buildTasks.problem: A very large statement can outlast a user's patience at the synchronous endpoint, and day-25 taught @Async - but a naive async import that changes the HTTP contract invents polling and status codes the course never taught, and ADR-012 deleted 202 Accepted for exactly that reason.
buildTasks.goal: An OPTIONAL path where the endpoint stays synchronous (HTTP 200 with the batch summary) and @Async is used only for a fire-and-forget notification (e.g. logging or a completion record update) after the batch finalizes - explicitly bounded, with an AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler.
constraints: the HTTP contract does NOT change: no 202 Accepted, no job status polling endpoint (ADR-012) - the endpoint stays synchronous and returns the same summary

the executor has an explicit bounded queue capacity in configuration
no 202 status, no polling endpoint, and no @Async call inside any row transaction exists

buildTasks.title: @Cacheable reference-data cache for read-mostly categories
buildTasks.problem: Category and reference lists are read on nearly every request but almost never change, so every page load re-queries them - the first legitimate cache subject Spendwise has, and also the first place a learner is tempted to cache a money value.
buildTasks.goal: A ConcurrentMapCacheManager-backed cache (final base per ADR-010) over category/reference reads via @Cacheable, with @CacheEvict on the category mutation paths, where no money value, balance or report total is ever cached (R11).
constraints: the cache manager is ConcurrentMapCacheManager (day-25 teaching, ADR-010 final base) - Redis is the separate optional task task-redis-cache-backend, not this one

@Cacheable on reference-data reads (categories), @CacheEvict on their write paths, with eviction placed so a read after a committed write never sees a stale value (day-25 blk-24 eviction-before-commit teaching)
NO money value, balance, budget figure or report total is ever cached (R11) - only non-financial reference data
the cache is non-authoritative: deleting the cache entirely must change no business outcome, only latency

read paths stay readOnly = true (R18); the cached object is the read model the service already returns (R16)

no cached type carries a money amount, balance or report total (inspect the cache contents in a test)
disabling caching entirely changes no test outcome except the cache-hit assertion

buildTasks.title: Scheduled balance-reconciliation job
buildTasks.problem: Account balances are a stored projection (R8), and projections drift when bugs or manual edits intervene - Spendwise has no mechanism that notices, so a drifted balance silently lies until a user complains.
buildTasks.goal: A bounded @Scheduled job (fixedDelay per day-25/day-27 teaching; if the schedule is ever expressed as cron, declare zone explicitly per day-25 blk-32) that periodically recomputes each account's balance from the transaction ledger and records/logs any drift - read-only detection with a defined outcome, never silent mutation.
constraints: the job runs on a bounded schedule: @EnableScheduling + @Scheduled(fixedDelay = ...) (day-25 blk-37) - never an uncontrolled loop; zone is a cron-only attribute (day-25 blk-32), so declare it explicitly only if the schedule ever becomes cron

single-threaded scheduler awareness: the job must not overlap itself or starve other scheduled work (day-25 blk-33 / day-27 blk-28 caveat - fixedDelay prevents overlap for consecutive runs of one method)

the reconciliation READS transactions and balances and RECORDS drift - it never mutates a balance directly, because balances change only through transaction rows (R21: balances are never mutated without corresponding transactions)
the invariant it checks is the V0.5 projection rule: balance == openingBalance + signed sum of the account's transactions (R6, R8)
no external calls or @Async dispatch inside the scheduled transaction (R19)
a run with zero drift produces a positive 'reconciled' signal; a run with drift produces a detectable record or log, not a silent pass
acceptanceCriteria: on a seeded consistent ledger the job runs and reports zero drift
a test that manually drifts one balance (repository-level, outside the canonical path) causes the next run to detect and report exactly that account
the job never edits a balance, transaction or budget row - verified by asserting no write occurs on a drift run
two consecutive runs cannot overlap (fixedDelay semantics, day-27 blk-28: consecutive runs of one method on one scheduler)

buildTasks.title: Scheduler wiring for recurring generation (idempotent by sourceRef)
buildTasks.problem: V0.7's RecurringGenerationService is a plain method a test must call by hand - real users expect rent to appear without opening the app, and an unguarded scheduler that re-runs generation is the classic way to double-bill.
buildTasks.goal: @EnableScheduling wiring that invokes the V0.7 generation service on a bounded fixedDelay schedule, relying on its deterministic sourceRef idempotency so a re-run for the same period creates nothing.
constraints: the scheduler CALLS RecurringGenerationService - no generation logic is re-implemented here; this task is wiring only (blueprint V0.9: 'recurring scheduler wiring')
the schedule is bounded: @Scheduled(fixedDelay = ...); no cron the learner cannot explain; no uncontrolled loop (day-25 blk-32: explicit zone is a cron-only discipline)
idempotency comes from the V0.7 deterministic sourceRef: a scheduler that fires twice in the same period creates exactly one transaction per occurrence (plan §9 flow 8)

the scheduler must not overlap itself (fixedDelay, day-27 blk-28's caveat: the guarantee holds for consecutive runs of one method on one scheduler; multi-instance deployment would need a distributed lock and is out of scope)
no external calls inside the generation transaction (R19); the scheduling method itself performs no I/O beyond invoking the service
acceptanceCriteria: with the scheduler active, a due monthly template generates its transaction without any manual invocation
firing the scheduled method twice back-to-back for the same period produces exactly one transaction per occurrence
the schedule is declared with fixedDelay in configuration, and the single-scheduler non-overlap caveat (day-27 blk-28) is documented
deactivating the template stops generation on the next tick

buildTasks.title: External exchange-rate WebClient with retry and failure handling
buildTasks.problem: Multi-currency display needs FX rates, but a slow or down external API must never take Spendwise's own endpoints down with it - and an FX rate that leaked into the ledger would violate the whole money model.
buildTasks.goal: A com.spendwise.fx ExchangeRateClient using WebClient (day-26) to fetch rates from an external API with bounded retry and explicit failure handling, exposed as display-only conversion in the report layer - never producing a ledger entry.
constraints: WebClient with a bounded timeout and retry (day-26 resilience teaching: retry with explicit max attempts/backoff, resilience4j or taught equivalents) - no unbounded retry, no blocking call inside a request path without a timeout

FX is display-only: conversion happens in the report/response layer and NEVER produces, edits or prices a ledger entry (R4)
no money value or rate is cached by the cache annotations of task-reference-data-cache (R11); the rate may be held in a plain service field/timeout-scoped holder with a documented freshness bound

buildTasks.title: Architecture-invariant unit test suite
buildTasks.problem: The Constitution's invariants (positive amounts, compareTo equality, derived-not-stored budget figures, no money cached, 404-not-403) live in prose and scattered tests - nothing systematically proves them, and a refactor that quietly breaks R7 would pass today's suite.

buildTasks.problem: The V0.4 endpoints and V0.5 repositories were tested end-to-end only; slice tests isolate the web layer from the persistence layer so a controller regression and a query regression stop masquerading as each other.

buildTasks.title: Final demo script and rehearsed walkthrough

buildTasks.title: Defense-readiness audit against the question matrix
buildTasks.problem: The final defense asks 'why' questions - why compareTo, why per-row atomicity, why no 202, why 404 not 403 - and answering them from memory under pressure fails where answering them FROM CODE succeeds; the audit turns the Constitution from something followed into something the learner can defend.

buildTasks.title: Optional AI category suggestion (advisory, off by default)
buildTasks.problem: Users categorize manually when no rule matches, and an LLM could suggest one - but an AI that writes categories directly would make a non-deterministic external system a writer of financial truth, which the whole architecture exists to prevent.
buildTasks.goal: An OPTIONAL advisory endpoint in an ai package that sends a transaction description to an LLM via WebClient (day-26/day-29 teaching) and returns a suggested category for the user to confirm - the suggestion is never persisted, and an accepted suggestion creates the transaction through the canonical path exactly as a manual one. acceptanceCriteria: with the flag off (default), the endpoint is absent/disabled and the full suite is green - no behavior change whatsoever
with the flag on and the provider up, a suggestion returns a category name without persisting anything

a provider failure or timeout yields an explicit no-suggestion response; no transaction, category or rule is created or edited by the AI path

with the flag on, the insight narrates figures that all match the dashboard response for the same month, verifiable by hand

buildSteps.doneWhen: integration tests prove: canonical creation end to end via TransactionCreationService with sourceRef; a forced mid-transfer failure leaves zero rows and unchanged balances; re-importing the same statement adds zero and reports DUPLICATE rows; two threads racing the same (user_id, source_ref) commit exactly one row
buildSteps.commonMistake: Mocking the creation service inside the integration suite to make setup easier - the suite exists precisely to test the real path; seed data through fixtures or the canonical service, never a bypass.

buildSteps.title: Add springdoc OpenAPI and spring-boot-starter-actuator, describe the API
buildSteps.intent: The API becomes self-documenting and observable: springdoc annotations on the real endpoints, Actuator health with database status.
buildSteps.doneWhen: springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui added with its explicit version (day-29 blk-3: 2.6.0 - not Boot-managed); /v3/api-docs describes the real endpoints; spring-boot-starter-actuator exposes /actuator/health reporting UP with database status via the taught HealthIndicator mechanism
buildSteps.mentorHint: Verify the two endpoints while the app runs (start it with .\mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run): the springdoc UI on /swagger-ui.html and /actuator/health showing db UP - then stop the app.

buildSteps.title: Add MDC traceId to request logging
buildSteps.intent: One request, one traceId: structured logging becomes actually usable when every line of a request shares its correlation id.
buildSteps.doneWhen: a servlet filter puts a generated traceId into MDC per request and clears it after; the logging pattern includes %X{traceId}; a test proves two log lines from one request share the id

buildSteps.title: Author the layered-jar Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml for app + postgres
buildSteps.intent: The reproducible run: layered Dockerfile per day-30, compose wiring app and database with configuration from environment - a second machine can now run Spendwise.
buildSteps.doneWhen: Dockerfile uses the layered-jar technique (extract layers, copy dependencies first); compose starts app + postgres with SPRING_DATASOURCE_* from environment and secret placeholders; docker compose up ends with the app's health check passing
buildSteps.verifyCommand: docker compose up --build -d; docker compose ps
buildSteps.commonMistake: Baking a real secret or the final JWT key into the image - environment placeholders only; the same discipline as the JWT secret applies to every credential.

buildSteps.title: Land the bounded async notification path with AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler
buildSteps.intent: The day-25 async subject finds its artifact: a fire-and-forget side effect after batch finalization - bounded executor, explicit handler, after-commit dispatch, no HTTP contract change.
buildSteps.doneWhen: bounded ThreadPoolTaskExecutor with explicit queue capacity; @Async notification dispatched after the batch is terminal (never inside a row transaction); AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler logs failures without altering batch state; the endpoint still returns the synchronous 200 summary

buildSteps.title: Generate and read the JaCoCo report (indicator, not a gate)
buildSteps.intent: Day-30's closing discipline: produce the coverage report, read it for the gaps it reveals, and resist turning it into a percentage gate.
buildSteps.doneWhen: the JaCoCo plugin (Boot-managed) generates target/site/jacoco/index.html on verify; the README records one honest observation from reading the report (a weak spot and why), with no percentage gate introduced
buildSteps.verifyCommand: .\mvnw.cmd verify; if (-not (Test-Path 'target\site\jacoco\index.html')) { Write-Host 'JaCoCo report missing'; exit 1 }; Write-Host 'JaCoCo report generated'

buildSteps.title: Add the optional Redis profile with explicit TTLs behind the same annotations
buildSteps.intent: ADR-010's sanctioned swap: Redis as an alternative cache manager selected by profile, with the @Cacheable/@CacheEvict surface untouched.
buildSteps.doneWhen: spring-boot-starter-data-redis added; a profile-guarded RedisCacheConfig provides RedisCacheManager with explicit per-cache entryTtl; the default profile still yields ConcurrentMapCacheManager; no annotation changes anywhere

buildSteps.title: Prove the swap: same tests green with Redis, nothing money-bearing cached
buildSteps.intent: A backend swap that changes behavior is a regression: the V0.9 cache tests must pass against both backends, and R11 must hold in both.
buildSteps.doneWhen: with the Redis profile active and Redis available, the cache-hit/eviction tests pass unchanged - RedisCacheSwapTest itself re-runs the cache-hit and eviction assertions from CategoryCacheTest against the Redis backend, so the single command exercises both backends; TTL expiry is observable; a test asserts no cache entry in either backend carries a money amount, balance or report total
buildSteps.commonMistake: JDK-serializing a record that will change shape next release - day-25 blk-26's trap; keep cached types serializable and stable, or exclude them and say why.

buildSteps.title: Build the multi-feature seeded-history fixture through legitimate paths
buildSteps.intent: The closing proof needs a history worth proving things on: months of data born through the canonical path, the import pipeline and the generation service - nothing raw-inserted.
buildSteps.doneWhen: a fixture seeds multi-month transactions across at least two accounts, budgets, recurring generations and one import batch - all through canonical paths - and a failing test asserts the reconciliation job reports zero drift over it

buildSteps.title: Run the full reconciliation and hand-computed SUM audit; fix what it exposes
buildSteps.intent: V1.0's purpose in one step: prove every derived figure matches hand-computed truth on a real history, and repair whatever the proof finds - through normal paths only.
buildSteps.doneWhen: hand-computed SUMs match dashboard, statistics and budget calculations over the seeded history; the reconciliation job reports zero drift; any exposed defect is fixed through normal paths with a regression test; no new architecture appears

buildSteps.title: Write the run section and verify it from a clean checkout
buildSteps.intent: The README's first obligation is that its instructions work: clone, configure, compose up, health green - proven, not assumed.
buildSteps.doneWhen: the run section carries the exact clone/configure/compose-up sequence; following it on a clean checkout ends with the app's health check green; the toolchain and pin-decision references match what the repo records

buildSteps.title: Narrate the architecture: invariants, decisions, identity model with its limitation
buildSteps.intent: The portfolio tells the truth about how the system is built - rule ids, ADR-level decisions, and the dedup limitation stated as plainly as the code states it.
buildSteps.doneWhen: the README narrates V0.1→V1.0, lists the Constitution invariants matching the rule suite's display names, records the key decisions (canonical path, per-row atomicity, no-202, 404-not-403, AI advisory), and describes import identity WITH the fallback-tier reordering limitation

buildSteps.title: Author the demo script over the composed app with invariant talking points
buildSteps.intent: The project's depth made visible in minutes: every segment executable, every segment naming the invariant it proves.
buildSteps.doneWhen: docs/demo-script.md walks: setup, account/category creation, transactions, import with a deliberate duplicate and malformed row, report, budgets, dashboard, idempotent re-import, health/docs, and a forced-failure rollback segment - each segment citing its rule ids and fitting a 10-15 minute window
